decisive_items: - CSF next-generation sequencing: positive for Candida tropicalis
CT scan of temporal bone showed otitis media, mastoiditis, and local bone destruction in the right ear
Figure 1B: Coronal contrast-enhanced MRI revealed heterogeneous enhancement in the dura and pia maters, with right thickened meninges extending to mastoid process
response.rationale: CSF NGS detected Candida tropicalis, and imaging shows contiguous otomastoid infection with meningeal involvement, making Candida meningitis the most specific infectious diagnosis. The anti-NMDAR/AMPAR antibodies support autoimmune encephalitis but do not explain the CSF organism or the ear-to-meninges route.

rejected.why: Otitis media and mastoiditis are the likely portal of entry but do not account for the meningeal/brain involvement.
Meningitis is too nonspecific once Candida tropicalis is identified in CSF.
Autoantibodies are present, but positive CSF Candida NGS and mastoid-to-meninges imaging favor fungal infection; autoimmunity may be secondary or incidental.
No peripheral neuropathy pattern is described; pronator drift and brain/meningeal findings indicate central disease, and diabetes is incidental.
